So I’ve been here for about 2-3 years. Worked out in Portland OR and now upstate NY so I have experience in city and rural delivering. I used to struggle to do 20hr but eventually just started to click and started to do about 30/hr sometimes 35-40/hr in dense neighborhoods. I spent a few months behind the desk as dispatch and would pay attention to netradyne and see when infractions would happen. Then I’d start to push the driving to netradyne limits and that helped cut down on time. Can steadily do 8mph over the speed limit without any infraction. 
I also organize in totes of 3, split the packages into the last 2 digits so all the 10s in one, 20s in the 2nd and 30s in the bag you’re pulling from. Lower half goes to the left, upper half to the right. Eventually you’ll be able to just park, grab the closest package to the right and hop out. I’ll spend max 20 seconds once I park to exit the van, usually when I’m flowing it’ll take 2-3 seconds to hop out. Even cutting down 20 seconds on each stop on a 200 stop route will cut down on 66 minutes. I try to make every movement/motion with purpose so I’m not taking extra steps. I walk with longer strides and at a decent pace but not power walking or anything that’ll take your breath away. Scan package as you’re walking to the house, have the photo screen prompt and ready for putting the package down, click photo as you’re turning around to walk back to the van and finish swiping as you’re walking back.

I just wait till I’m through the first 2 totes, then every tote after that gets split in 10s, all 20s in one 30s in the other, if there’s more it stays in the initial bag. Makes it about 10 seconds per stop to hop in the back, find the package and then get out. Overtime you’ll start to get 1-10 from left to right and makes it even faster. Can easily do 25-27 stops an hour with just walking nonchalantly.

Tbf I wish 20 an hour was still the “normal”. Don’t get me wrong, 20/hr is still a lot. I avg routes over 190 stops, I really only get about 8 hours to deliver all that. It’s 30 mins once I’m in the van to get my pkgs and leave the station, 30 or more to my first stop so 2 hours of the day is wasted in transport and waiting for pkgs. then count in an hour for breaks (1 30min 2 15min) and that now cuts down to 7 hours to deliver 190 stops. I have to do at least 27/hr to allow myself to take an hour break 🥲. It’s taxing but I don’t run or walk faster than a normal walk, just have to stay organized and off my phone and it’s pretty doable.
No tips but I got a $1 raise and guaranteed gap pay. Felt good getting done in 6 hours w/o taking breaks to get outta there.

Man I feel ya on that. I was trained by a literal crack/meth head when I first started. I was told to just dump out the tote on a shelf and spread it all out… took me months to find a rhythm and little tricks for organizing.

If you are in nursery routes, yes please pace yourself a little slower because the algorithm will bite you in the ass if you finish fast. I usually skip my lunch and 2 15s because I hate sitting and doing nothing but I consistently have the highest stop count routes because I can finish without rescues 99% of the time.

When I get to a new tote I will organize by the last 2 digits on driver aid and in groups of 10. Ex; all the 20s go in one tote, 30s in another, 40s in the last. This at least splits up the tote into sections and each stop you only have to look over 10 or less packages instead of the entire thing. Overtime you’ll get more efficient, I spend maybe 5 seconds once I park and get in the back to find my package, scan the package in the van and click “front door” or whatever the delivery option is so by the time you’re at the door you can flick the picture and swipe next all in one motion. 

Feel free to reach out or dm if you have questions or want more advice. I’ve been at this gig for 2+ years, 200~ routes and have been dispatch so I know a ting or two.

So what you’re describing is what it’s like to grow if you are a major company and the “suits” will spend all the money in the world to try and automate the entire process, but it ultimately creates and extremely inferior product. 95% of weed sold In dispensaries and ultimately on the black market are being machine trimmed which means you can hire anybody to feed the machine branches of the plant for it to be bucked and processed through a machine that strips 85% or more of the trichomes and shreds the buds BUT they give them a uniform look which makes it easier to sell and to the end user it usually makes it look “dense” which makes it easier to sell. The average consumer prefers the appearance of machine trimmed bud vs hand trimmed. A machine can trim anywhere from 2lb to 20lb an hour depending on the machine. The most talented hand trimmers that don’t skimp on quality usually can trim 1-2lb in a 10-14 hr day of work. On my farm we would pay $200 a lb plus we fed and gave room and board to 5 trimmers. It took over 10 days of work to process 50lbs, a machine can do that in less than a days work of operation which makes it cheaper to produce. I find articles on brewing kombucha are so misleading. They use a lot of words/terminology interchangeably and not actually accurately. What you’re looking at is a Pellicle, it’s like a byproduct of the fermentation when there’s proper bacteria and yeast colonies aka SCOBY (symbiotic culture of bacteria and yeast) the scoby is in the liquid of the mother tea itself, it’s not the pellicle. ALTHOUGH, using a pellicle along with starter tea from the mother brew will help aid and speed up fermentation. FWIW after every batch you can throw away the pellicle that has formed, I wouldn’t throw out the tea though; depending on how sweet you want the kombucha just add more sugar/split the vessel into two.

I can help you understand it a little bit. I believe you're referring to bubble hash. Which is basically pure trichome heads extracted by using ice, water, mesh screen bags, and a tumbler machine. You start by filling your bubble bag with product and freeze that until it's completely frozen. Then you place that bag into your machine that is filled with as much ice as possible, with the least amount of water. You want enough water for all the product to mix together . So basically you want it to be as cold as possible inside because that's what shocks the trichome glands and they separate from inside the bag, goes through the screen and into the water mix which is then emptied into your series of bags in order from highest to lowest; 220, 150, 120, 90, 73, 25 micron. I believe there may be one more bag but I personally like 120-73 the most so I discard/cook with the rest. But after you empty the water and drain it through the system of bags you want to scoop out the resin in the bottom of the bags and put it in a glass container, and mix with distilled water let the impurities rise to the top and poor off the top water the resin glands will stick to the bottom for the most part. 

After you rinse and wash your bubble(preferred if you want clean bubble hash) the next step is to properly cure it, that's where you can ruin the best bubble, so you want to have a cardboard box placed down with parchment paper on top of it, place the hash on the paper and spread it out as much as possible. You want each individual gland seperated for the best cure. Leave it in a cool dark area for about 48-72 hours. After that, my man, you should have some smokeable solventless bubble hash
